prompts.prompt:
Create a detailed educational infographic for a backend developer learning UI/UX, landscape 1536x1024 or larger. Editorial vector-like illustration, very legible Segoe/Inter style type, cool white #f8fbff, cobalt #245bd6, light blue #e7f0ff, navy #132f55. Semantic green and amber only for status. This is a new illustration, not a screenshot.
Title exactly: "A usable screen answers the next question."
Central large invoice management application mockup taking left two-thirds: title Invoices, supporting text Track payments, one solid blue New invoice button, outlined Export button, search field labelled Customer and a Status filter, readable table Invoice / Customer / Amount / Status, three rows including Paid and Overdue text badges. Small mobile layout inset showing stacked invoice summary with same actions.
Around screen, numbered markers connected by clear short leaders to six concise callouts:
1 "Purpose" / "What can I do here?"
2 "Hierarchy" / "One primary action"
3 "Grouping" / "Filters beside their data"
4 "Readable data" / "Aligned amounts + status words"
5 "Keyboard" / "Visible focus + real controls"
6 "Responsive" / "Same task on a narrow screen"
At bottom, three equally sized detailed state mini-panels with distinct heading and visual:
"Loading" shows stable skeleton rows and Loading invoices…;
"Empty" shows No invoices yet and Create invoice button;
"Error" shows Could not load invoices and Try again button.
Small footer: "Review structure, behavior and accessibility before polish."
Keep every text label crisp, no overlapping leaders, no random icons, no gradients, no watermark. Enough whitespace for reading but more explanatory detail than a decorative poster. Use no invented metrics or certification badges.

Create a precise, detailed educational infographic for a backend developer, landscape 1536x1024 or larger. Clean editorial vector-like diagram with restrained blue palette: cool white #f8fbff, cobalt #245bd6, pale blue #e7f0ff, navy #132f55. Large readable typography. Two horizontally separated lanes, equal visual weight, strong titles, clear arrows.
Main title exactly: "Two places an AI agent can work"
TOP LANE title "1 · While you build the software".
Three stages: "Your task" with example "Improve invoice screen" → "Coding agent" shown using three small inputs "Skill instructions", "Repository context", "Editor + browser tools" → "Reviewable change" with code diff and test check illustration.
Small caption below this lane: "Taste, Impeccable, Web Design Guidelines and VSA guide the coding agent."
BOTTOM LANE title "2 · Inside the running product".
Three stages: "User request" example "Investigate an unpaid invoice" → "Runtime agent" with a simple loop of "Choose a tool" → "Read result" → "Decide next step" returning to Choose a tool → "Answer or draft".
Under runtime lane a smaller guardrail strip with three labelled checkpoints: "Allowed tools", "Step + time limits", "Approval before sending".
Bottom emphasized takeaway: "A skill is guidance. A model call is not automatically an agent."
Small supporting footer: "Spring AI supplies integration building blocks; your application owns the workflow."
Use small illustrative documents, tools, code diff, invoice; avoid robots, sci-fi, fake logos, decoration. Exact labels, no duplicated or truncated text, no ambiguous arrow crossing. Make the two contexts and their outputs visibly different.
